value: This article provides an intuitive exploration of Milnor fibrations, mathematical maps defined by complex polynomials. It explains their construction and demonstrates how their four-dimensional "fibers" can be visualized in three dimensions through stereographic projection, analogous to an "open book decomposition." The discussion primarily illustrates how the singular set of the Milnor map forms a bounding knot or link (e.g., trefoil, Hopf link) for these fibers. Furthermore, the article delves into the theoretical connection between the parameters of the defining polynomial and the specific topological type of the resulting singular knot, particularly its relation to torus knots.
